en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīya (2), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 8.1.
Hetuduka (The Pairs on Causes)
The Cause:
Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
Dependent on a causeless state, a causeless state arises by way of the cause-condition: dependent on one causeless aggregate...
Dependent on [one] aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and mind-produced matter.
At the moment of rebirth-linking … (up to the great primary elements).

Dependent on a state that is not a root-cause, there arises a state that is not a root-cause by way of root-condition: dependent on rootless aggregates, there arise root-causes; at the moment of rebirth-linking … (as above).
...pe... dependent on a state that is not a root-cause (nahetu), states that are both not-root-causes and not non-root-causes arise by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya).
Dependent on a state that is not a root-cause, a state that is not a root-cause arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is not a root-cause, a state that is a root-cause arises by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state that is not a root-cause, states that are both [not-root-causes and] root-causes arise...
Non-causal states arise with a cause-condition.

Dependent on both non-causal and non-non-causal states, a non-causal state arises with a cause-condition. Dependent on both non-causal and non-non-causal states, a non-non-causal state arises with a cause-condition.
Dependent on both non-causal and... [non-non-causal states, a non-causal state arises with a cause-condition]. Non-causal and... [non-non-causal]...
Dependent on a non-root phenomenon, both non-root and non-non-root phenomena arise by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
There are nine [instances] for root; nine for object … pe … nine for non-disappearance.
(The section on co-nascence … pe … and the section on association should also be expanded in this same manner, just like the section on dependence.)
Root-object condition:

A state that is not a root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is not a root. A state that is not a root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is not a root.
A state that is not a root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is both not a root and not a non-root.
Condition by way of root-cause (hetu-paccaya).
A state that is not a root-cause (na-hetu dhammo) is a condition for a state that is not a root-cause by way of object-condition (ārammaṇa-paccaya).

A state that is not a root-cause is a condition for a state that is not a non-root-cause by way of object-condition. A state that is not a root-cause is a condition for a state that is both a root-cause and not a root-cause...
Conditioned by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya).

A state that is not a root-cause (na-hetu) is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is not a root-cause. A state that is not a root-cause is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is a root-cause.
A state that is not a root-cause is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is both a root-cause and not a root-cause.
And [these] states are a condition for a state that is not a root-cause by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).
States that are both not-root-causes and not-not-root-causes are a condition for a state that is not a root-cause by way of object-condition.
States that are both not-root-causes and not-not-root-causes are a condition for a state that is not a root-cause by way of object-condition. [States that are] not-root-causes and...
States that are not-root conditions are related to states that are not-root conditions, and to states that are not-root conditions, by way of the object-condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root: three; under object: nine ... [etc. ... under prenascence and postnascence: three ... [etc. ... under kamma: three ... [etc. ... under jhāna: three ... [etc. ...
under dissociation: five ... [etc. ... under non-disappearance: nine. (It should be expanded in detail just as the section on questions in the wholesome triad.)
